territorial_scope.description: Regulations of a California state agency applying to businesses subject to the CCPA as defined under California law.

evidence.quote: In addition to the definitions set forth in Civil Code section 1798.140, for purposes of these regulations:

summary.short: California Privacy Protection Agency regulations implementing the CCPA: privacy policy, notice, consumer request, opt-out, service provider contract, non-discrimination, minors and cybersecurity audit duties for covered businesses, plus automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) rules; timing varies by provision.
summary.long: Regulations issued by the California Privacy Protection Agency (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, § 7000 et seq.) under the California Consumer Privacy Act. Article 1 defines terms, including automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) and significant decisions, and limits collection and use of personal information to reasonably necessary and proportionate purposes. Articles 2 to 4 require privacy policies, notices at collection, opt-out and limit notices, handling of consumer requests (confirmation within 10 business days; response within 45 calendar days, extendable to 90), opt-out preference signals, and contract terms for service providers and third parties. Article 5 sets identity verification rules; Article 6 sets parental consent rules for consumers under 13; Article 7 restricts discriminatory price or service differences; Article 8 requires request metrics from businesses handling personal information of 10,000,000 or more consumers. Article 9 requires cybersecurity audits for businesses above processing thresholds, with first reports due by April 1, 2028 for businesses with 2026 gross revenue above $100,000,000. The table of contents also lists sections on risk assessments, ADMT pre-use notices, opt-out and access rights, insurance companies and sworn complaints; their operative text is not in the part of the document provided here.

notes: Part 1 covers §§ 7001 to 7121 (definitions through cybersecurity audit timing); the ADMT provisions and remaining articles are expected in part 2. The text is a redline extract in which deleted and inserted wording appear together (e.g., duplicate lettering such as '(f) (e)' and '(ccc) (ii)', and alternations such as 'may must', 'shall. shall'). Sentences were annotated as printed; struck wording was not coded. The definition lettering is inconsistent, so provisions are cited by definition name where needed. Civil Code sections cited throughout are treated as one instrument; hypothetical 'Business' examples are not entities. Part 2 of 2 covers §§ 7122-7124, 7150-7157, 7200, 7220-7222, 7270-7271, 7300 and 7302. Relations list citations to other laws only; references to sections of this Title 11 text are not listed. Drafting residue: § 7300(a) reads 'Sworn complaints may must be filed'; § 7302(b) reads 'The Enforcement Division Agency'; § 7302(c)(3) reads 'appear at attend'; § 7123(c)(17)(A) refers to 'subsection (17)'. § 7155(b) contains the placeholder '[OAL to fill in the effective date of these regulations]', so this part gives no effective date. § 7155(b) sets a December 31, 2027 deadline for certain existing processing. Standards bodies named in § 7122(a) (AICPA, PCAOB, ISACA, ISO) are not designated and are not listed as entities.

“Automated decisionmaking technology” or “ADMT” means any technology that processes personal information and uses computation to replace human decisionmaking or substantially replace human decisionmaking.
to “substantially replace human decisionmaking” means a business uses the technology’s output to make a decision without human involvement.
Human involvement requires the human reviewer to:
“Profiling” means any form of automated processing of personal information to evaluate certain personal aspects

“Significant decision” means a decision that results in the provision or denial of financial or lending services, housing, education enrollment or opportunities, employment or independent contracting opportunities or compensation, or healthcare services.
“Performance at work” means the performance of job duties for which the consumer has been hired or has applied to be hired.
“Performance in an educational program” means the performance of coursework in an educational program

definitions.term: Physical or biological identification or profiling

evidence.quote: “Physical or biological identification or profiling” means identifying or profiling a consumer using automated measurements or analysis of their physical or biological characteristics
“Systematic observation” means methodical and regular or continuous observation.

“Train” for the purposes of sections 7150, subsection (b)(6), and 7153 means the process through which a technology discovers underlying patterns, learns a series of actions, or is taught to generate a desired output.
“Sensitive personal information” means:
“Cybersecurity audit” means the annual cybersecurity audit that every business
“Information system” means the resources (e.g., network, hardware, and software) organized for the processing of personal information or that can provide access to personal information.

means the time and/or resources expended by the business, service provider, contractor, or third party to respond to the individualized request significantly outweighs the reasonably foreseeable impact to the consumer by not responding
“Financial incentive” means a program, benefit, or other offering, including payments to consumers, for the collection, retention, sale, or sharing of personal information.

“Price or service difference” means (1) any difference in the price or rate charged for any goods or services to any consumer related to the collection, retention, sale, or sharing of personal information
“Value of the consumer’s data” means the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data as calculated under section 7081.

“Opt-out preference signal” means a signal that is sent by a platform, technology, or mechanism, on behalf of the consumer, that communicates the consumer choice to opt-out of the sale and sharing of personal information
“Frictionless manner” means a business’s processing of an opt-out preference signal that complies with the requirements set forth in section 7025, subsection (f).
“Right to opt-out of ADMT” means a consumer’s right to direct that a business not use ADMT with respect to the consumer
“Right to access ADMT” means a consumer’s right to request that a business provide information to the consumer about the business’s use of ADMT with respect to the consumer
“Nonbusiness” means a person or entity that does not meet the definition of
“Employment-related information” means personal information that is collected by the business about a natural person
using a qualified, objective, independent professional (“auditor”)
“security incident” means an occurrence that actually or imminently jeopardizes the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the business’s information system
A “comparable set of processing activities” that can be addressed by a single risk assessment is a set of similar processing activities that present similar risks to consumers’ privacy.
For purposes of this paragraph, “intends to use” means the business is using, plans to use, permits others to use
A business that makes ADMT available to another business (“recipientbusiness”)
“Infer or extrapolate” does not include a business using a consumer’s personal information solely to deliver goods to, or provide transportation for, that consumer at a sensitive location.
A change relating to the processing activity is material if it creates new negative impacts or increases the magnitude or likelihood of previously identified negative impacts

evidence.quote: shall comply with the CCPA with regard to any personal information not subject to the Insurance Code

obligations.summary: A sworn complaint filed with the Agency must identify the business or person alleged to have violated the CCPA, state supporting facts and evidence, authorize communication with the alleged violator, include the complainant's contact details, and be signed under penalty of perjury.
obligations.conditional_on: Complaint filed with the Agency

evidence.quote: A complaint must:

obligations.summary: The Enforcement Division must notify the complainant in writing of the action, if any, the Agency has taken or plans to take, with reasons.
obligations.conditional_on: Sworn complaint filed with the Agency

evidence.quote: The Enforcement Division will notify the complainant in writing of the action

obligations.summary: The Agency must give the alleged violator notice of the probable cause proceeding, conduct the proceeding informally (closed to the public unless the alleged violator requests otherwise), determine probable cause on the record, and issue a written decision that is final and not subject to appeal.
obligations.conditional_on: Probable cause proceeding under Civil Code section 1798.199.50

evidence.quote: The Agency shall issue a written decision with its probable cause determination

obligations.summary: Notices of probable cause and probable cause determinations must not be open to the public or admissible in evidence in any action other than one enforcing the CCPA.
obligations.conditional_on: Probable cause notices and determinations

evidence.quote: Notices of probable cause and probable cause determinations shall not be open to the public nor admissible in evidence

enforcement.note: Part 2 contains Article 13 (§§7300-7302) on sworn complaints and probable cause proceedings, which are procedural. It states no fine, penalty maximum, criminal penalty, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. Penalty provisions are referenced only as Civil Code §§1798.199.45 and 1798.199.50, which are not in this text. Other articles in part 2 contain no sanctions.
